Earning Experience

At the end of each session, every character receives one to three Experience Traits, based on the player's performance and involvement in the story. The Narrator decides the award:

  • Automatic (1 Trait): Every player receives at least this much for participating — representing the acquisition of common, everyday knowledge.
  • Roleplaying (up to 2 Traits): Exceptional roleplayers who played a memorable part receive a second Trait.
  • Leadership (up to 3 Traits): Characters who performed acts of real insight and courage, or whose efforts drove the story forward, may receive a third Trait. If multiple players showed this kind of leadership in the same story, each should be awarded the Trait.

On a typical night, expect one Experience Trait per character.

Spending Experience

Experience Traits purchase new Abilities, Traits, and Disciplines, improving a character over time. Exact costs as printed in the rulebook:

PurchaseCost
New Attribute Trait (Physical/Social/Mental)1 Experience per Trait
New Ability Trait, levels 1–51 Experience per Trait
New Ability Trait, levels 6–102 Experience per Trait
New Background Trait1 Experience per Trait (Storyteller approval required; Backgrounds may also rise or fall purely through roleplaying)
New Discipline — Basic power3 Experience
New Discipline — Intermediate power6 Experience
New Discipline — Advanced power9 Experience
Out-of-clan Discipline surcharge+1 Experience added to the power's normal cost
New Humanity/Path Trait2 Experience per Trait (Storyteller approval required)
New MeritDouble the Merit's listed Trait cost (Narrator approval; should be worked into the character's ongoing story, not bought instantly)
New Necromancy or Thaumaturgy Ritual — Basic2 Experience
New Necromancy or Thaumaturgy Ritual — Intermediate4 Experience
New Necromancy or Thaumaturgy Ritual — Advanced6 Experience
New Ability Specialization1 Experience Trait (must already hold a level in the Ability)
New Virtue Trait3 Experience per Trait (must also tie into the character's ongoing story)
New Willpower Trait3 Experience per Trait
Buy off a Negative Trait2 Experience per Trait
Buy off a FlawDouble the Flaw's listed Trait cost (Storyteller approval; worked into the story)

Storyteller Guidance on Awarding Experience

  • Be consistent and fair, and award Experience openly — be ready to explain your rationale.
  • If players disagree with an award, hear them out, confirm the full story, then award what's earned.
  • Awarding too much Experience makes characters too powerful too fast and breeds complacency; awarding too little discourages players and damages their sense of achievement. Aim for the middle.
  • Track each player's Experience awards and expenditures directly on her character sheet, updating it regularly (ideally reviewed a day or two before each session).
